newsitem.title: RUSSIA: U.S. activity moves some Russian shares.
newsitem.headline: U.S. activity moves some Russian shares.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed mixed on Friday as the market picked up in late trading when U.S. investors spurred activity, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 23 shares edged up by 1.35 percent to 299.06 on a low $26.10 million total market volume.

"We opened with a rise on remainders from late yesterday's trade, then there was a fall and quiet. With the New York opening we started rising smoothly," said Troika Dialog senior trader Alexei Dolgikh.
St Petersburg Telephone ordinaries slipped to $1.55 from $1.59 at Thursday's close after the company said it would issue 44.1 million preferred shares and 2.5 million ordinary shares this year.
St Petersburg Telephone shares were $1.05 after $1.10.
Brunswick trader Gary Kinsey forecast the share might fall further. "Obviously it is bad news for the stock so I think we can see it come back a little bit," he said.
Norilsk Nickel ordinaries edged down to $5.01 from $5.30 and preferred shares were $3.45 after $3.63.

Dolgikh attributed the fall to the news that the company had decided to double the capital of its flagship plant and transfer the new controlling stake to the government as part of a plan to restructure tax arrears.
Moscow power utility Mosenergo edged up to $1.307 from $1.267, national power grid UES rose to $0.2205 from $0.2185 and LUKoil was $13.69 after $13.60.
